title: Watchogue
summary: An East Moriches neck placename, with a related Islip use west of Bay Shore.
ancestral_territory_note: Shown in relation to Unkechaug Ancestral Land on the current ancestral territory map.
why_this_matters: Watchogue preserves a Native place name for a neck of land in East Moriches, bounded by Mattuck brook and Pomiches creek. The takeaway is that place names can work like compact maps: they hold geography, memory, and local knowledge that later town names or casual labels like "the neck" often flatten or replace.
introduction_content: Watchogue is a neck of land at East Moriches, Brookhaven Town. This neck contains the east section of the village of East Moriches, and is locally known as the "neck." Watchogue is bounded on the east by "Mattuck" brook and west by a creek named "Pomiches."
history_content: At East Moriches, Watchogue names a neck between Mattuck Brook and Pomiches Creek. A related Islip use west of Bay Shore is represented separately through the Manetuck record, showing how similar names could appear in more than one south-shore landscape.
translation_content:
Recorded forms include Watchogue, Watchauge, and Watshage. The name is interpreted as hill land or land on a hill.

Why Place Names Matter

“Indigenous place names are shared amongst the community and are used when travelling or telling stories.”

— Alestine Andre, Ingrid Kritsch, Kristi Benson, and Sharon Snowshoe, An Indigenous Place Names Handbook: Sharing the Gwich’in Experience in Canada (2023), Executive summary, printed p. vi; PDF page 7
preservation_content: Watchogue preserves a hill-land name attached to necks and boundary waterways in both East Moriches and Islip.
whereintheworld_content: Blue/general approximate marker on the East Moriches neck between Mattuck Brook and Pomiches Creek. This is not an exact deed-boundary coordinate.
